subject: Weekly capacity sync: Artemis pilot GPU commitment triage
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nadia Patel <n.patel@artemishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Dec 2029 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Weekly capacity sync: Artemis pilot GPU commitment triage

Team —

Ahead of tomorrow’s capacity huddle I wanted to surface where Artemis sits against our conservative/target commit bands and get alignment on what we plan to lock this week. Attached: a quick heatmap and a proposed commitment PDF. Key points: 

- Forecasted peak (Jan–Mar): 3,600 GPU-days/month (signal from their prod test harness).
- Sales ask (pilot -> early production): 900 GPU-days/month preferred reserve tranche for Q1; they want predictable latency targets.
- Our current slot availability (conservative pool): 650 GPU-days/month if we exclude burst and canary capacity.

Asks for this thread: 
1) Ben — please confirm the burn projection you want us to use for pricing (attached).
2) Laura — can finance provisionally sign off on the 900 -> 650 gap impact to committed revenue recognition and any suggested holdbacks?
3) Karthik — are there infra constraints (kernel availability / pool isolation) that would block a 900 commit? If so, what’s the realistic ramp?

Plan I’m proposing: agree a short-term signed commit at 650 GPU-days/month (reserved) with a 60-day escalation clause to add burst slots if Artemis hits agreed throughput. Use the canary strategy (quantized variant) for initial traffic to reduce risk.

Attachments: artemis-pipeline-heatmap.csv, commit-proposal-v2.pdf

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Sofia + all —

I ran a short projection and attached an XLSX with three scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Highlights: 
- Conservative (what we model for reserved pricing): 650 GPU-days/month (aligns with Sofia's conservative pool).
- Expected: 900 GPU-days — this assumes a 2x concurrent batch peak for scheduled scoring windows.
- Aggressive: 1,500 GPU-days if they onboard two enterprise customers in Jan.

Pricing note: the per-GPU-day rate in the commit-proposal-v2 PDF is built off the conservative model; if we sign at 900 we'll need to move to tiered pricing because burn > threshold.

Open points for the huddle: 
- Which tranche do we recommend for canary vs reserved vs burst? I'm proposing: 50% reserved (immediately), 30% burst-on-demand, 20% canary/quantized.
- If finance can only approve 650 for signoff, we should include an explicit addendum for a 60-day ramp clause and a pre-agreed conversion to tiered pricing at 900.

Attachment: ben-burn-projections.xlsx

—Ben

Folks —

Finance quick take: we can provisionally approve a 650 GPU-days/month committed slot for Q1 with the following caveats:
- We need a signed term sheet with a clear ramp schedule and a cap on our exposure (max 3 months of committed liability on our balance sheet before conversion).
- Any reserved->burst conversion needs to be pre-authorized via an ops ticket and tagged to deal DL-4821 for revenue attribution.
- Suggest a 10% holdback on the first invoice until Artemis completes the compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence + data-retention attestation).

If Ben expects to be at 900 within 45 days we can fast-track an amendment to add the additional tranche once the operational signals hit (utilization > 70% for two consecutive weeks).

I’ll attach a short note capturing the above and the finance approval language. Once legal has the signature-ready term sheet Laura will forward to DocuSign.

Attachment: finance-approval-note.pdf

All —

Infra check and runbook pointers below. Short version: 650 reserved is fine to commit now; 900 is feasible but requires a sequencing plan to avoid kernel contention across pools. Notes: 

- Current pool utilization across the us-west cluster is ~68% for Jan forecasted baseline. We have capacity to allocate 650 GPU-days without bumping other high-SLA customers if we reallocate two low-priority burst racks.
- For the 900 scenario we need: (a) scheduling window that spreads heavy batched runs to off-peak hours, (b) enable the quantized (int8) model variant for 30% of requests during the canary, (c) 48-hr scaling buffer to recompile kernels for persistent pinned pools.
- Operational action items for the bridge call:
  * Create a dedicated p2 pool: tag: dl-4821-p2 (ops ticket #OPS-11948).
  * Enable prefix caching for the pilot to reduce repeated KV traffic — reduces effective GPU-days by approx 8–12%.
  * Fallback: if we see sustained >85% utilization for 5 days, auto-failover to tiered quantized serving in a different region (eu-west) for non-latency-critical batch jobs.

Runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=runbook-scaling-2029Q4
DocuSign (term sheet): https://docsend.com/doc/Artemis-Docusign-link-4821

If finance signs off on the 650 commit (with holdback language), I’ll create the ops ticket and schedule a 30-minute provisioning window next Tuesday to pin the pool and run the kernel compilation job.

—Karthik
